Why auto layout is changing Auto layout was designed to mirror how the web renders layouts, but a few edge cases never quite matched CSS. This meant that hand-off from design to code (and code to design) sometimes required workarounds—like using a negative-offset outline to fake a border, or manually double-checking that a frame's padding actually fit inside its bounds. sources.excerpt: hy properties You’ll find the most common text properties in the Typography section of the right sidebar. Use the image below to identify each property. Click the property name to learn more about each property. View the list of properties and links Select to create and apply text styles . Select the font name to browse a list of web fonts, fonts installed on your computer, and shared fonts to find a typeface or font family . Select a font weight or style. Adjust the font size of your text. Use line height to adjust the vertical distance between lines of text. Use letter spacing to adjust the horizontal distance between letters. Adjust the horizontal alignment of text within the text box. Adjust the vertical alignment of text within the text box. Click to open the type settings panel and explore more text properties. Looking for the text resizing property? You can update resizing for text layers in the Layout section of the right sidebar. Learn more about text dimensions and resizing . Type setti … perty to see the preview. Figma displays sample text based on the feature you're previewing. This includes: Blocks of text for alignment, spacing, and indentation. Numerals for number properties. Letters (or combinations of letters) affected by ligatures or stylistic alternatives. Basics Detail Variable Adjust the horizontal alignment of text. Apply decoration to text, like strikethrough and underline. Adjust the letter case . Choose from uppercase, lowercase, capitalize, and small caps. Toggle vertical trim . Create numbered or bulleted lists . Change the spacing between paragraphs of text. Toggle Truncate text to hide any content that goes beyond the maximum number of lines. Set the maximum number of lines to determine when your text will be truncated. Select a Wrap style to control where lines break when text wraps to more than one line. Adjust Indentation settings: Adjust paragraph indentation to offset the first line of text in a paragraph. Toggle hanging quotes Toggle hanging lists Use Letter … the horizontal alignment. Choose from: Left Center Right Justify* Justify aligns the first word in each line of text to the left-most edge, and the last to the right-most edge. Figma spaces each word in a line of justified text uniformly. Vertical alignment aligns text along the y axis (vertical) . Use the alignment icons to select a vertical alignment. Choose from: Top Middle Bottom Note: It's only possible to vertically align text in text layers with a Fixed Size . Layers with resizing set to Auto Width or Auto Height will ignore alignment. Decoration Apply text decoration to an entire text layer, or to selected text. You have two types of decoration available: Strikethrough Underline Strikethrough Underline Strikethrough adds a horizontal line through the center of your text. Use strikethrough to indicate obsolete or inaccurate information. This allows you to convey its state, without redacting or obscuring the original text. Click the icon to apply strikethrough to selected text. Under … ypeface. Adjust the letter spacing for an entire text layer, or a selection of text. To replicate kerning, place the cursor between two letters and adjust the letter spacing. Use the field to adjust letter spacing for your selection, or use the keyboard shortcuts: Mac : Hold down ⌥ Option and < to increase or > to decrease. Windows : Hold down Alt and < to increase or > to decrease. If you select text with different letter spacing values, Figma will scale the letter spacing proportionally. Tip! Tracking describes the letter spacing process in the manual printing process and is usually represented in 1/1000em. One unit of tracking (1/1000em) is approximately equal to 0.001em letter-spacing (CSS). You can use this formula to convert tracking to letter spacing: letter spacing = tracking/1000 . Line height Line height allows you to control the vertical distance between lines of text in a paragraph. This can help to balance designs and improve the readability of your copy. This is the same as line … reduce the whitespace around text in your design. White space can help to focus the viewer's attention, as well as increase legibility and readability. Figma represents paragraph spacing in pixels (px) . Enter a px value in the Paragraph spacing field. Or hover above the icon and drag to decrease (left) or increase (right) the value. Note: Figma will create a new paragraph when you use the Enter or Return keys. This is something to bear in mind if your text resizing is set to Auto Width . Text truncation and max lines Truncate text hides text that overflows the bounding box. An ellipsis ... is added at the end of the text to indicate hidden overflow text. Max lines allows you to set the number of lines of text before it truncates. Max lines is available only if truncate text is enabled, and: Text resizing is set to auto height or auto width Vertical resizing is set to hug contents (for text living in auto layout frames) Vertical trim Use vertical trim to remove the extra space above and below t … tespace around text in your design. White space can help to focus the viewer's attention, as well as increase legibility and readability. Figma represents paragraph spacing in pixels (px) . Enter a px value in the Paragraph spacing field. Or hover above the icon and drag to decrease (left) or increase (right) the value. Rate limits & access Figma MCP Server Introduction On this page Introduction The Figma MCP server brings Figma into your AI workflow. It gives AI agents the design context they need to generate code from your Figma files, and lets agents write native Figma content back to the canvas. MCP servers use the Model Context Protocol , a standard interface that lets AI agents interact with data sources. What you can do with the Figma MCP server ​ Let your agent write directly to the canvas in Figma Design, FigJam, and Figma Slides Create and modify native Figma content from your MCP client. With the right skills, agents can build and update frames, components, variables, and auto layout in your files, using your design system as the source of truth. note Note: This feature requires the remote Figma MCP server and a Full seat to write outside your drafts. It's free during the beta period and will eventually become a usage-based paid feature. Learn more about writing to the canvas Generate designs from the live UI of your web apps and sites Turn live UI from your browser (production, staging, or localhost) into editable design layers. Send pages, elements, or whole flows to Figma Design for exploration, alignment, and refinement. note Note: This feature requires the remote Figma MCP server and is supported by select clients. Learn more about generating designs from your interfaces Generate code from selected frames Select a Figma frame and turn it into code. This is useful for product teams building new flows or iterating on app features. Extract design context Pull variables, components, and layout data into your IDE. This is especially useful for design systems and component-based workflows. Retrieve FigJam resources Use content from your FigJam diagrams in your code generation workflow, so early-stage ideas, flows, and architecture maps carry into development. Retrieve Make resources Gather code resources from Make files and provide them to your agent as context. This helps as you move from prototype to production. Keep generated code consistent with Code Connect Improve output quality by reusing your actual components. Code Connect keeps generated code consistent with your codebase. Learn more about Code Connect Give your agent project context with Figma Specs Use the figma-spec skill to let your agent read, create, and update your team's specs. Share requirements before your agent starts building, and have it capture decisions and discoveries back in the spec as it works. Note: Figma Specs is in open beta. Writing to a spec requires the remote Figma MCP server and edit access to the file. Learn more about the figma-spec skill Write to canvas and code to canvas are continuously being improved. If you run into issues, report them using Fig, our support chatbot , or by emailing support (paid plans) . note The MCP server and Figma Agent can access fonts uploaded to your account. Learn how to add a font to Figma. Set up the MCP server ​ You can connect to the Figma MCP server in two ways: Remote MCP server (recommended) : Connects directly to Figma’s hosted endpoint at https://mcp.figma.com/mcp , without the Figma desktop app. The remote server offers the broadest set of features and is the best choice for most users. Learn how to install the remote MCP server. Desktop MCP server : Runs locally through the Figma desktop app . The desktop server is intended for specific organization and enterprise needs. It requires a Dev or Full seat on a Professional, Education, Organization, Government, or Enterprise plan . Learn how to install the desktop MCP server. For information about usage and rate limits, see Plans, access, and permissions . note Figma for Government supports the desktop server only. See Figma for Government for available tools and current limitations. If you plan to write to the canvas, also install Figma’s skills for your MCP client. Skills help your agent use the write tools more reliably and follow the right workflow when creating or updating content in Figma. Connect the MCP server to your editor ​ Follow the instructions for your editor to connect to the remote or desktop server. Some clients also support skills , which add agent-level instructions that help AI tools work more effectively with Figma designs. If you're a developer who wants to connect a new MCP client, join the waitlist . About skills ​ Skills tell an agent how to complete specific tasks, combining MCP tool calls with detailed instructions. The Figma MCP server exposes individual tools; skills help agents understand which tools to use, in what order, and how to apply the results. Skills can guide agents through workflows like: Connecting Figma design components to code components with Code Connect Generating design system rules aligned to your codebase Translating designs into production-ready code Reading and updating Figma Specs, so your agent works from your team's requirements Skills don’t replace the MCP connection or add new capabilities. They reduce setup and guesswork by packaging recommended workflows into reusable instructions. To learn more about skills: Use skills with the Figma MCP server Figma skills for MCP note Skills are also available from the Figma Community and through community contributions in the Figma community-resources repo on GitHub. items.name: Code Connect 2.0.2
items.summary: ## Features ### General - Code Connect publishing on Professional plans now confirms the active library and framework when they are first selected. If a publish exceeds the one-library, one-framework limit, the CLI explains the restriction and how a plan admin can change the selection or upgrade. - `figma connect publish` now sends preflight validation failure counts to Figma. Set `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` to disable this telemetry. ## Fixed ### General - `figma connect migrate` now leaves existing template files unchanged and reports success when no components need migrating. - Fixed Code Connect file discovery in project folders whose names contain special characters, while preserving configured file exclusions and project-relative includes with a leading slash. - Network request failures now include the underlying reason, such as a timeout or a connection error, instead of only showing "fetch failed". Run the command with `--verbose` to see the stack trace. - `figma connect create` now always generates a parserless template file, including in projects configured for a framework-specific parser. items.name: Code Connect 2.0.1
items.summary: ## Fixed ### General - `figma connect preview` now accepts the template file of a component declared in a `.figma.batch.json` file. Previously it rejected the template path with "Not a valid Code Connect file", so the only way to preview a batch component was to preview every component in the batch file at once.

items.name: Code Connect 2.0.0
items.summary: > [!WARNING] > Framework-specific parsers will no longer receive updates or support. Template files are now the only actively maintained way of using Code Connect. See our migration guide for more information and instructions on migrating parser-based Code Connect: > https://developers.figma.com/docs/code-connect/templates-migration-guide/ ## Breaking changes - Framework-specific parsers can now only be used by `figma connect migrate` and `figma connect unpublish`. Other commands exit with guidance to migrate parser-based Code Connect to template files. If you wish to continue using framework-specific parsers, install Code Connect v1 with `npm install --save-dev @figma/code-connect@1`. ## Fixed ### General - Performance optimizations for `figma connect preview`

items.name: Code Connect 1.5.3
items.summary: ## Fixed ### React - Fixed rendering of nested arrow function callbacks ## Features ### General - Adds `figma connect preview <file> --unique`, which is similar to `--all` but hides duplicate outputs. ### Template files - Added `id` to `InstanceHandle` to expose the instance's Figma node ID. items.name: Code Connect 1.5.2
items.summary: ## Fixed - Fixed JavaScript template files authored with `import figma from 'figma'` publishing an unexecutable import.

items.name: Code Connect 1.5.0
items.summary: > [!WARNING] > Previously, Code Connect required framework-specific parsers for React, iOS, Android and Web Components. Late in 2025, we introduced a new [template API](https://developers.figma.com/docs/code-connect/template-api/) that removed framework requirements and allows users to more flexibly control how code snippets are rendered inside of Figma. Going forward, new users should opt for this template format and we recommend existing users to follow our [migration guide](https://developers.figma.com/docs/code-connect/templates-migration-guide/) to move to the new format. Following August 17th, 2026, we will no longer be updating or actively maintaining the legacy parsers. ## Fixed ### Template files - Fixed nested rendered examples being dropped or formatted incorrectly when interpolated directly or passed to the React, Swift, and Kotlin child-rendering helpers. - Migrated template files no longer include unused generated prop constants. ## Features ### Template files - Added a `--delete` option to `figma connect migrate` that deletes source Code Connect files after they are successfully migrated. - Template files (TypeScript and JavaScript) now support importing local helper modules via relative paths (for example, `./shared-helpers`) to promote reuse of shared formatting and utility logic. Helper code is bundled into the published template so it can run standalone, and helpers may import other local helpers to organize shared logic across multiple files. Only relative imports within the project are supported (external packages are not), and helpers must be brought in with `import` syntax — `require` remains available for the Figma API itself. Helper code you don't actually use is left out of the published template, and if the bundled output exceeds the maximum template size, the CLI fails before publishing. ### General - `figma connect preview` can now render a component in states beyond its default, and inspect its properties: - `figma connect preview <file> --inspect` prints the component's properties and variants — name, type, variant options, and default — without rendering a snippet. - `figma connect preview <file> --props Name=Value …` renders a single specific property combination. Pairs are space-separated arguments (quote a pair only when its name or value contains spaces, e.g. `"Has Icon Start=true"`). Property names and variant values are matched case-insensitively, unspecified properties keep their defaults, and an invalid variant value is reported along with the valid options. To target a property when two properties share a name but differ in type, prefix the pair with the type, e.g. `"BOOLEAN:textMsg=false" "TEXT:textMsg=Hello"`; the prefix is optional and only needed to disambiguate. - `figma connect preview <file> --all` renders every property combination of the component — the cartesian product of its variant and boolean properties. Requires a specific component file argument. Use `--max-combinations <number>` to render fewer combinations when the full set is large.

items.name: v1.4.9
items.summary: ## Fixed ### General - Fixed parser invocation failing when a path or argument contained a space. This affected the Swift parser (Xcode project / Swift package paths), the Compose parser (Gradle wrapper paths), and the custom parser (any user-provided `parserCommand` referencing a path with spaces). ### Template files - Fixed template-only projects unnecessarily building and running a native parser. When every Code Connect file is a parserless template (`.figma.ts`/`.figma.js`), the CLI no longer invokes the Swift or Compose parser — which is slow at best and can fail outright (for example a Swift package targeting macOS 12 whose `Figma` dependency requires macOS 13, producing "the library '...' requires macos 12.0, but depends on the product 'Figma' which requires macos 13.0"). Projects that also contain native source files are unaffected and still run the parser. ### Swift - Raised the supported `swift-syntax` upper bound to allow the 603.x release. Previously the cap below 603 could silently downgrade `swift-syntax` in projects that depend on both Code Connect and `swift-syntax` (directly or transitively) on a Swift 6.3 toolchain. Older toolchains remain supported. ## Features ### General - Added `@figma/code-connect/figma-types-no-require`, a variant of the template type definitions for projects that have `@types/node` installed. The default `@figma/code-connect/figma-types` entry declares a global `require` (so `const figma = require('figma')` works without `@types/node`), but that declaration overrides Node's own `require` type and causes errors like `Property 'resolve' does not exist` on `require.resolve(...)` elsewhere in projects that use `@types/node`. Such projects can now use `"@figma/code-connect/figma-types-no-require"` in their `types` array instead, adding it to their main `tsconfig.json` without a separate config. The default entry is unchanged, so no existing setup needs to change. ### Template files - Augmented the `getSlot` API: `getSlot('SlotName')` still renders the same way, and the returned value now also exposes `connectedInstances` (the connected instances directly in the slot). This lets you render a slot's connected children inline. For example `getSlot('body').connectedInstances.map((c) => c.executeTemplate().example)`. ### React & HTML - Augmented the `figma.slot` API: `figma.slot('SlotName')` still maps the slot the same way, and you can now also write `figma.slot('SlotName').connectedInstances` in a `props` object to render the slot's code-connected instances inline. For example `props: { content: figma.slot('Content').connectedInstances }`.

items.name: Code Connect 1.4.8
items.summary: ## Fixed ### General - Fixed browser compatibility issues where importing `@figma/code-connect` in Storybook or webpack environments would fail with "Can't resolve 'child_process'" or "Console is not a constructor" errors. Node.js-only modules (`child_process`, `console`) are now imported dynamically only when needed by CLI commands, making the package safe to use in browser environments. ### Template files - Fixed template projects failing to publish or parse when Code Connect could not infer a React, HTML, Swift, or Compose parser. The CLI now proceeds without a parser and uses the default template-file globs. - Fixed a "`getInstanceSwap(...)?.executeTemplate is not a function`" error that could break a template when `getInstanceSwap('prop')` referenced an instance-swap property that isn't present on the selected node (for example a property that is conditionally hidden by a boolean). The missing property now renders an inline error, consistent with the other accessors, instead of failing the whole template. - Fixed migrated text-layer references (from the React/HTML `figma.textContent('...')` helper) producing a TypeScript error and silently rendering nothing when the layer was missing. Migration now preserves the original behavior — the text renders when the layer is found, and a clear error is shown when it isn't. ## Features ### Template files - The `figma connect migrate` command now uses the same `--dir` and `--file` filtering behavior as `publish`, `parse`, and `unpublish`. The migrate-only positional glob argument has been removed. - The `figma connect migrate` command can now migrate compatible large source files into batch template files. Files with 10 or more Code Connect docs are attempted automatically, `--batch all` forces a batch attempt, and `--batch none` disables batch migration.

items.name: Code Connect 1.4.7
items.summary: ## Fixed ### General - The `--file` (`-f`) option on `figma connect publish`, `unpublish`, and `parse` now accepts multiple files, so you can target several Code Connect files in one command (e.g. `figma connect publish --file a.figma.ts b.figma.ts`). Previously only a single file path was accepted. - Tweak retry behavior for `publish` command to reduce 429s errors - Shared flags (`--verbose`, `--token`, `--config`, `--dir`, `--file`, `--out-file`, `--out-dir`, `--api-url`, `--skip-update-check`, `--exit-on-unreadable-files`, `--dry-run`) now work whether you write them before or after the subcommand name. Previously, only `figma connect publish -v` toggled verbose mode; `figma connect -v publish` was silently ignored. ### Compose - Fixed a crash that prevented the Code Connect Gradle plugin from being used with projects on Kotlin 2.3 or newer. The plugin now runs Kotlin source parsing in an isolated worker process, so it no longer ships an embedded Kotlin compiler in the consumer's build environment and cannot conflict with the host project's Kotlin Gradle Plugin across version upgrades. - Fixed `parseCodeConnect` / `createCodeConnect` failing in multi-module Gradle projects when the plugin is applied to more than one subproject. The task now resolves the `-PfilePath`/`-PoutputDir` arguments against the root project so every subproject finds the input the CLI wrote at the build root. - The Code Connect Gradle tasks now work cleanly with Gradle's configuration cache enabled. Previously, enabling `--configuration-cache` caused an opaque serialization error; the tasks now store and reuse the configuration cache entry as expected.

items.name: Code Connect 1.4.5
items.summary: ## Fixed ### General - The `preview` command now prints a clearer single-line message if the preview service is temporarily unavailable, instead of repeating a per-file error. - `figma connect preview` now splits requests into smaller chunks when previewing many components at once, so previews of large component libraries no longer fail with “Payload Too Large” errors.

items.name: Code Connect 1.4.4
items.summary: ## Fixed ### General - Bumped Lodash version from 4.17 to 4.18 to address vulnerability [CVE-2021-23337](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=) ### Storybook - Storybook files with `.ts`, `.jsx`, or `.js` extensions (e.g. `Button.stories.jsx`) are now discovered by the CLI. Previously only `.stories.tsx` files were picked up. ### Template files - `--exit-on-unreadable-files` is now respected for template files (`.figma.ts` / `.figma.js`) - Fixed batch data not being picked up when rendering Code Connect snippets ## Features ### General - Added `--force` flag to `figma connect publish`. When Figma already has UI-created Code Connect mappings for one or more nodes, publishing will now show a warning instead of failing silently. Use `--force` to overwrite those existing mappings with the Code Connect files from your codebase. - The `connect create` command can now generates template files. - Added `preview` command: you can now run `npx figma connect preview {fileUrl}` to locally preview a Code Connect file without having to publish it. ### Template files - Added batch template support (`.figma.batch.json` + `.figma.batch.ts`). A batch file defines a shared template and an array of component entries, allowing hundreds of similar components (e.g. icons) to be Code Connected without individual template files. Per-entry data is available in the template via `figma.batch`.

items.name: Code Connect 1.4.3
items.summary: ## Fixed ### Template files - Fixed `getBoolean()` returning `undefined` instead of `false` when a boolean property is set to `false` in a template file. - Fixed some TS discrepancies in the `figma.*` API in template files - Some fixes for the migration script ### Swift & Compose - Fixed args inconsistency in Swift and Compose helpers that could cause errors during template rendering. ## Features ### CLI - Added `--file` (`-f`) option to `parse`, `publish`, and `unpublish` commands to process a single Code Connect file instead of the entire project (e.g. `figma connect parse --file=src/Button.figma.tsx`). ### Template files - The `migrate` command now outputs TypeScript (`.figma.ts`) files by default. Pass `--javascript` to output JavaScript (`.figma.js`) files instead. - The `migrate` command now outputs `import figma from "figma"` (ESM syntax) when using the `--typescript` flag - The `migrate` command now removes `__props` metadata blocks by default. Pass `--include-props` to preserve them. - Storybook connections can now be migrated by the template migration script

sources.excerpt: Specification - Model Context Protocol Documentation Index Fetch the complete documentation index at: /llms.txt Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further. Skip to main content Model Context Protocol home page Version 2026-07-28 (latest) Search... ⌘ K Ask Assistant ⌘ I Blog GitHub Discord Search... Navigation Specification Documentation Specification Extensions Registry SEPs Community Specification Key Changes Deprecated Features Architecture Base Protocol Overview Versioning and Compatibility Message Patterns Transports Authorization Client Features Roots Sampling Elicitation Server Features Overview Discovery Prompts Resources Tools Utilities Schema Reference On this page Overview Key Details Base Protocol Features Additional Utilities Extensions Security and Trust & Safety Key Principles Implementation Guidelines Learn More Specification Copy page Copy page Copy page Copy page Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open protocol that enables seamless integration between LLM applications and external data sources and tools. Whether you’re building an AI-powered IDE, enhancing a chat interface, or creating custom AI workflows, MCP provides a standardized way to connect LLMs with the context they need. This specification defines the authoritative protocol requirements, based on the TypeScript schema in schema.ts . For implementation guides and examples, visit modelcontextprotocol.io . The key words “MUST”, “MUST NOT”, “REQUIRED”, “SHALL”, “SHALL NOT”, “SHOULD”, “SHOULD NOT”, “RECOMMENDED”, “NOT RECOMMENDED”, “MAY”, and “OPTIONAL” in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 [ RFC2119 ] [ RFC8174 ] when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here. ​ Overview MCP provides a standardized way for applications to: Share contextual information with language models Expose tools and capabilities to AI systems Build composable integrations and workflows The protocol uses JSON-RPC 2.0 messages to establish communication between: Hosts : LLM applications that initiate connections Clients : Connectors within the host application Servers : Services that provide context and capabilities MCP takes some inspiration from the Language Server Protocol , which standardizes how to add support for programming languages across a whole ecosystem of development tools. In a similar way, MCP standardizes how to integrate additional context and tools into the ecosystem of AI applications. ​ Key Details ​ Base Protocol JSON-RPC message format Stateless, self-contained requests Per-request capability negotiation ​ Features Servers offer any of the following features to clients: Resources : Context and data, for the user or the AI model to use Prompts : Templated messages and workflows for users Tools : Functions for the AI model to execute Clients may offer the following features to servers: Elicitation : Server-initiated requests for additional information from users ​ Additional Utilities Configuration Progress tracking Cancellation Error reporting ​ Extensions Beyond the core protocol, MCP defines optional extensions that add modular, specialized, or experimental functionality. Extensions are always opt-in and require explicit support from both client and server, negotiated during initialization. Notable extensions include: Tasks : Asynchronous execution of long-running operations, with polling, mid-flight input, and durable handles Skills over MCP : Rich, structured instructions for agent workflows, discovered and consumed through MCP MCP Apps : Interactive UI elements (charts, forms, video players) rendered inline within conversations ​ Security and Trust & Safety The Model Context Protocol enables powerful capabilities through arbitrary data access and code execution paths. With this power comes important security and trust considerations that all implementors must carefully address. ​ Key Principles User Consent and Control Users must explicitly consent to and understand all data access and operations Users must retain control over what data is shared and what actions are taken Implementors should provide clear UIs for reviewing and authorizing activities Data Privacy Hosts must obtain explicit user consent before exposing user data to servers Hosts must not transmit resource data elsewhere without user consent User data should be protected with appropriate access controls Tool Safety Tools represent arbitrary code execution and must be treated with appropriate caution. In particular, descriptions of tool behavior such as annotations should be considered untrusted, unless obtained from a trusted server. Hosts must obtain explicit user consent before invoking any tool Users should understand what each tool does before authorizing its use ​ Implementation Guidelines While MCP itself cannot enforce these security principles at the protocol level, implementors SHOULD : Build robust consent and authorization flows into their applications Provide clear documentation of security implications Implement appropriate access controls and data protections Follow security best practices in their integrations Consider privacy implications in their feature designs ​ Learn More Explore the detailed specification for each protocol component: Architecture Base Protocol Server Features Client Features Contributing Was this page helpful? sources.title: v2.1.309

items.name: v2.1.309
items.summary: ## What's changed - Fixed sandboxed Bash commands on macOS and Linux running the shell's startup files outside the sandbox before each command - Fixed macOS sandbox `denyWrite` glob patterns not applying at a path's real location when the pattern's folder is reached through a symlink - Fixed sandboxed commands and auto-accepted edits being able to modify the MCP config file passed with `--mcp-config` - Fixed a disabled MCP server being reconnected by a later permission prompt in print and SDK sessions - Fixed the Bash permission check trusting a variable set by a command whose redirect can fail to open - Fixed Bash permission checks not prompting for some compound commands that change directory before running git when the `cd` is wrapped or prefixed, as they do for a plain `cd` - Fixed an `Edit(path)` deny rule not blocking a Bash redirect to that path in some commands that also held a subshell - Fixed worktree-isolated sessions accepting some locale-prefixed commands the isolation guard should refuse - Fixed worktree-isolated sessions on zsh accepting some arithmetic commands that the isolation guard should refuse - Fixed worktrees and branch checkouts that Claude Code creates so they ignore git replace refs, as its other git operations already do - Fixed profile store write protection not applying when the config directory is reached through a symlink - Fixed sessions compacting repeatedly after reading files under a very large nested CLAUDE.md; a nested CLAUDE.md over the size limit now loads only its start - Fixed ctrl+enter (send now) only queuing a message when pressed before the response had started, and restarting a prompt's hooks while leaving the message queued when pressed while those hooks were running - Fixed key-bound slash commands running in the shell from `!` mode - Fixed ctrl+o not showing messages from other agents and sessions that are still waiting to be delivered; they now appear in full under the transcript, marked as waiting - Fixed long tool output previews being cut through an emoji, leaving session transcripts that `jq` could not parse - Fixed Read reporting "File does not exist" for PDF page ranges in Linux sandboxes that share the parent's `/proc` - Fixed messages from a Claude Desktop-hosted session sometimes being lost when its connection refreshed - Fixed features missing from Claude Code sessions in the Claude desktop app when the terminal on the same computer was signed in to a different account or organization - Fixed the `claude remote-control` status line showing `HEAD` as the branch for a folder that is not in a git repository - Fixed split-pane agent teammates not inheriting the tool deny and `--tools` rules given on the leader's command line - Fixed sessions renamed with `/rename` appearing to other sessions under a generated name after a VS Code window reload or a non-interactive `--resume` - Fixed the `/rewind` list showing "No code changes" for a turn that changed checkpointed files through `/code-review --fix`, a subagent or a shell command - Fixed `/privacy-settings` showing an out-of-date "Help improve our AI models" value; it now also says when the setting can't be fetched - Fixed feedback saying "try again later" when your organization does not accept feedback; it now shows the server's reason and where to report a bug - Fixed oversized /feedback reports failing instead of being resent without the transcript - Fixed a skill in an `--add-dir` folder being unreachable when another skill already held its name; it is now offered as `<folder>:<name>` - Fixed `/verify` and `/code-review` not finding a nested package's own skill when its files were changed from the shell - Fixed the /claude-api skill saying that `ant beta:worker poll --on-work` passes trace context to the command - Fixed the /claude-api skill's C# tracing setup missing spans from the cloud platform clients - Fixed the /claude-api skill saying that API spans for requests to Claude Platform on AWS can't join the caller's

items.name: v2.1.308
items.summary: ## What's changed - Bug fixes and reliability improvements

items.name: v2.1.307
items.summary: ## What's changed - Added `/claude-api api-version` to move Claude API code to API version `2026-10-21` - Added the `claude_code.safety_event` OpenTelemetry event for each tool call a permission rule, auto mode, a safety check, a hook or the sandbox stopped, prompted or sent back - Fixed requests failing with a model-not-found error when `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_1M_CONTEXT` is set and the model is an alias with the `[1m]` suffix, such as `opus[1m]` - Fixed the `prompt-caching-scope` beta header being sent behind custom `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` gateways and on Foundry, where it has no effect - Fixed MCP servers showing "needs authentication" in `claude -p` on macOS while the login keychain was locked; they now say why, and the next run after an unlock connects without a new sign-in - Fixed MCP servers being reported as timed out, and staying failed in headless runs, when a macOS or Linux computer went to sleep while they were connecting - Fixed HTTP MCP tool calls being sent twice when the connection closed mid-call; only read-only or idempotent tools are now retried - Fixed a turn sometimes starting without an SDK MCP server's latest tools when a background task was running - Fixed some "Autocompact is thrashing" errors in turns that read many PDF pages, images or other large tool results - Fixed `/autocompact` in cloud sessions going back to the default window after the session restarted - Fixed a conversation cleared with `/clear` sometimes coming back when a cloud or self-hosted runner session restarted - Fixed `CLAUDE_STREAM_FIRST_BYTE_TIMEOUT_MS` being ignored in Claude apps gateway sessions - Fixed telemetry from Claude Desktop sessions behind a Claude apps gateway being rejected when `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS` is set - Fixed `/permissions` > Recently denied not showing the denied shell command, and auto mode's local classifier ignoring an approval from there when it checks a retried command; approving a row now names the command, not its description - Fixed `/help` and the `/` command menu showing long model-facing descriptions for bundled skills such as `/claude-api` instead of their short descriptions - Fixed subagent transcripts recording placeholder token usage and an empty stop reason for streamed responses - Fixed model switches through the Agent SDK's `setModel()`, and apps built on it, being refused when the API took more than 5 seconds to confirm the model; Claude Code now waits up to 15 seconds - Fixed a background command stopped through a connected app (such as the desktop app archiving an idle session) being reported to Claude as stopped by the user; the notice now names its output file - Fixed WebFetch in Cowork cloud sessions reporting a tool error when a site answered with a 4xx status or a robots.txt refusal; it is now a normal result, as in local sessions - Fixed write tools on a directly configured GitHub MCP server showing a form that closed without creating anything in the desktop app's Code tab - Fixed Artifact tool reads failing with a connection reset when the server had closed a reused connection - Self-hosted runner: Fixed sessions with `--use-anthropic-git-proxy` committing a `.claude/settings.local.json` left in the clone by an earlier session - Self-hosted runner: Fixed archiving or requeueing a session, or stopping the runner, during its checkout hook leaving the hook's processes running and the runner's slot held - Improved recovery from unparseable tool calls: Claude Code now retries the call up to twice before ending the turn with an error - Improved fork subagents launched together: each is now told which launch is its own, so forks are much less likely to try to start each other's work - Improved browser sign-in: the success page now appears as soon as sign-in completes, without waiting for your account profile to load - Improved web search errors in cloud and self-hosted runner sessions: a search refused with a 403 that gives a reason now shows that reason instead of a generic "Authenticati

items.name: v2.1.306
items.summary: ## What's changed - Fixed `claude -p` inside cloud sessions reporting "Not logged in" when started without the session's environment variables - Fixed an API error being replaced by "prompt is too long", and an unneeded compaction, in sessions with many MCP tools

items.name: v2.1.305
items.summary: ## What's changed - Added `sandbox.allowNestedUserNamespaces` so sandboxed commands on Linux can create user namespaces (Chromium, rootless podman); this lets them get around the sandbox's file protections - Added `CLAUDE_CODE_RETRY_WATCHDOG_USAGE_LIMIT_RECHECK_MS` so unattended retry mode (`CLAUDE_CODE_RETRY_WATCHDOG`) notices a usage limit that was lifted before its reset - Fixed every request failing on Vertex, Bedrock and other providers when the endpoint or a gateway rejects tool search, and behind gateways with ToolSearch disallowed or left out of `--tools` (a 2.1.304 regression): Claude Code now retries without it - Fixed `/effort` and `/autocompact` settings not applying when the model name differed from a `modelOverrides` value by letter case or a `[1m]` tag - Fixed new worktrees in a bare repository sometimes starting from local HEAD instead of the default branch, and unchanged subagent worktrees sometimes not being cleaned up - Fixed Bash commands on a full disk failing with a raw `ENOSPC` file path: the error now says the disk is full and that nothing ran - Fixed an MCP server passed by a cloud session or by the SDK's `setMcpServers` being replaced later in the session by a same-named server from your own settings - Fixed Claude naming the wrong model for a subagent's work after the subagent switched to a fallback model - Fixed cloud sessions and teammates not telling Claude when a compaction had to leave the oldest messages out of its summary to fit - Fixed more cases of scheduled Cowork cloud sessions waiting five minutes for each subagent whose WebFetch needed a URL approval that nobody was there to give - Fixed Workflow resume re-running already-completed `pipeline()` and `parallel()` agents instead of serving them from the run's journal - Fixed Remote Control leaving empty "(session)" entries in `/resume` after switching conversations with `/resume` - Fixed `/usage` rows being cut off in narrow terminals - Fixed startup warnings printing as raw text above the logo: they now go to the debug log, and permission rules that restrict nothing show as warning rows under the banner - Fixed screen reader mode: search boxes now say "Search:" instead of a symbol VoiceOver read as "telephone recorder", and highlighted prompt text, such as Ctrl+R search matches and "ultrathink", no longer has spaces inside words - Self-hosted runner: Fixed a start script that shares only its stdout with the runner or orchestrator failing with `Resource temporarily unavailable` when `TERM` is set (a 2.1.300 regression) - Self-hosted runner: Fixed repository access failing since 2.1.296 when a git credential helper or askpass program reads its settings through `GIT_CONFIG` - Self-hosted runner: Fixed the orchestrator reporting a spawn-runner hook as timed out when a runner it started in the background kept its output open - Improved `/usage`: each warning is now a one-line fix that names its source, and `f` applies the fixes; the same fixes appear in VS Code and `/doctor` - Improved MCP consent dialogs so an Enter meant for the prompt is less likely to be taken as Accept - Improved a mod's `Image` to draw its picture in iTerm2 3.5 and later with fullscreen rendering, where it showed only its `alt` text - Remote Control: Improved the spawn-mode messages: pressing `w` now says the new mode is saved for the folder, and a later `claude remote-control` start that uses the saved mode says where it came from - Changed `allowedMcpServers` to stop filtering `managed-mcp.json` stdio servers that use `${VAR}` only in `env`: one your allowlist left out now loads on upgrade; use `deniedMcpServers` to keep it off - Changed plugins that Claude Desktop mounts by path to no longer keep their `allowed-tools` when your organization's managed settings set `allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly` - Changed the `/artifacts` delete confirmation to take 1 or Enter to keep, 2 to delete, and Esc to cancel; `y` and `n` no longer answer it - Changed a mod's docked pane to sta

items.name: v2.1.304
items.summary: ## What's changed - Added a transcript line when a plugin that runs first skips one of your mod's hooks, naming the event and the plugin - Added `decider: "person"` to a mod's `tool.check` answer: only the permission dialog or a host's callback can approve the ask, and it is refused with the mod's reason where nobody can be asked - Added `e.isReadOnly` to a mod's `tool.check` event, set when the tool call is read-only - Added `/auto-mode-setup`: a guided setup that reads your project and recent sessions to teach auto mode about your environment, now also available on Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry, Claude apps gateway and telemetry-disabled sessions - Added `/claude-api managed-agents-secure`, which compares a Managed Agents agent's settings with Anthropic's published security guide, without changing anything - Added the names of the tools called earlier to the compaction summary in the transcript view (Ctrl+O) - Added a warning on Pro and Max plans when resuming an inactive conversation would use a noticeable share of your 5-hour usage limit: resume anyway, or start a new conversation and Claude can look up the previous one if you refer to it - Fixed the organization policy not refreshing until the hourly check after approving an `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` at startup or switching "Use custom API key" in `/config` - Fixed sandboxed commands failing to start on Linux when a `sandbox.filesystem.denyRead` glob contains brackets that are not a character class, such as a `[user-id]` route folder - Fixed `rm -r` of a mounted drive or a folder at its top level (`/Volumes`, `/media`, WSL's `/mnt/c`) not getting the safety prompt that `rm -rf /Applications` gets - Fixed `CLAUDE_CODE_TRANSCRIPT_LOCAL_GC` dropping messages from the saved transcript when the disk filled up while the file was being trimmed - Fixed a plugin keeping a headless run going past `--max-turns`, Stop, or ended input by spawning subagents or re-running a finished one - Fixed a failed mod reload removing the tools and commands of the version that stays loaded, and its messages being wrong or silent about whether the previous version is still loaded - Fixed a click on a mod's button being lost when buttons with the same label and no `key` were redrawn unchanged - Fixed mod sharing in the built-in `plugin-authoring` skill stopping at the secret scan on machines with managed settings and on Team and Enterprise plans - Fixed scheduled Cowork cloud sessions waiting five minutes again for each subagent whose WebFetch needed a URL approval that nobody was there to give - Fixed Write results and rejected edits showing a file outside the working directory as `../../…`; they now show `~/…` or the full path - Fixed a claude.ai Directory plugin's skills not running as commands when picked from the "/" menu in Cowork cloud sessions - Fixed Remote Control permanently withholding a desktop conversation's history when a different account was signed in to the terminal - Fixed Remote Control failing to start from Claude Desktop when DISABLE_TELEMETRY or DO_NOT_TRACK is set on a paid plan - Fixed model switches, messages and interrupts waiting behind a context usage check in SDK and desktop sessions - Fixed `context_management: Extra inputs are not permitted` errors behind LLM gateways; Claude Code now resends the request without that field - Fixed OpenTelemetry settings delivered through server-managed settings being ignored for the whole session after signing in during first-run setup or the first start after /logout - Fixed unsandboxed Bash commands in Claude Desktop Code tab sessions on macOS and Linux not seeing environment variables exported in shell startup files such as ~/.zshrc - Fixed the Consumer Terms notice being skipped for a day or longer after a server error - Fixed `/privacy-settings` offering choices that may not apply to you after a network or server error - Fixed a "Context limit reached" or "Prompt is too long" error after stopping a turn while Claude Code was compacting a con

items.name: v2.1.303
items.summary: ## What's changed - Bug fixes and reliability improvements

items.name: v2.1.302
items.summary: ## What's changed - Added `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_MODE_MODEL` to choose the model the client-side auto mode classifier uses; it does not change the model for server-side auto mode - Added an `Idle compaction` row to `/config` for turning idle compaction off or back on; the notices shown after an idle compaction now say how to turn it off - Added a notice to `/design-sync` and `/design-login` that standalone Claude Design (claude.ai/design) closes by December 14, 2026 - Fixed a "Prompt is too long" error when stopping a turn while the conversation was being compacted - Fixed requests failing with "diagnostics: Extra inputs are not permitted" after switching to Vertex or Bedrock mid-session - Fixed the Read tool loading an image file of any size, or a pipe or device named like an image, entirely into memory; image sources over 128 MB are now refused - Fixed `/autocompact` and `/effort` saving to the wrong model when a gateway names Opus 4 or 4.1 with a prefix, such as `anthropic/claude-opus-4-1` - Fixed a prompt cache miss when a tool added mid-session was loaded again through ToolSearch or after compaction - Fixed `claude plugin` and other subcommands sometimes exiting before a queued settings or config write finished, which could lose the change or leave a `.tmp` file behind - Fixed plugin marketplaces re-cloning on every refresh, and newly installed git plugins showing version "unknown", when git defaults to the reftable ref format - Fixed the PowerShell tool not finding commands in a plugin's `bin/` folder, and reporting an error when a search that finds nothing (rg, grep, findstr, git grep) is piped into `Select-Object` or another formatting cmdlet - Fixed Claude in the desktop app pointing you to claude.ai settings or `/mcp` to authorize or reconnect an MCP server where that option isn't available - Fixed artifact publishes sometimes failing when Claude sent an empty list of edits, and Claude retrying an artifact update the wrong way after a newer version of the artifact turned it away - Fixed `classifier_category` missing from OpenTelemetry `tool_decision` events for most auto mode classifier blocks, and new `tool_decision` attributes pushing out `tool_use_id`, `tool_source` and `tool_parameters` when `OTEL_LOGRECORD_ATTRIBUTE_COUNT_LIMIT` is low - Fixed rows in the agents view staying blank after moving down a long list or folding a section - Fixed `claude remote-control --help` not printing its usage and exiting when not signed in - Fixed `/design consent` and `/design revoke` suggesting `/design-login` when they fail in a cloud session, where it isn't available; the message now points to claude.ai/design/settings - Fixed MCP servers showing no tools, or every tool call failing, when the server negotiates protocol version 2026-07-28 but omits `resultType`, `ttlMs` or `cacheScope` - Fixed prompt suggestions spending usage credits on models your plan pays for only with credits: they are now skipped after a reply billed to credits - Fixed URLs written in backticks being clickable only on their first row when they wrap; the whole URL is now one link in terminals that support hyperlinks - Fixed `claude plugin details <name>@builtin` suggesting `claude plugin list`, which never shows built-in plugins, when the plugin isn't found; it now points to `/plugin` - Fixed an emoji that a link starts inside wrapping one column too wide, which hid it in question previews and turned tables into lists - Fixed worktree isolation refusing to create or resume worktrees under git 2.56 or later when a stray `.git` file points at a directory that doesn't exist - Fixed a cloud session's cost and usage restarting from zero after the session resumed in a new process - Self-hosted runner: Fixed git fetches failing with "bad object refs/heads" in sessions that reuse a checkout stored in git's reftable format - Windows: Fixed every file write being refused or asked about for projects on exFAT or FAT32 drives, including in sessions started with `--plugin-d

items.name: v2.1.301
items.summary: ## What's changed - Added `CLAUDE_CODE_RETRY_WATCHDOG_MAX_USAGE_LIMIT_WAIT_MS` so unattended retry mode (`CLAUDE_CODE_RETRY_WATCHDOG`) ends a request at a usage limit that resets too far away instead of waiting - Added OpenTelemetry tracing guidance to the `claude-api` skill, including setting up trace destinations with the `ant` CLI - Added the `%` motion to vim mode: jump to the matching bracket, alone or with d/c/y -
